rationale: The round-0 candidate compiled and ran correctly, so the table is tuned toward stronger obfuscation while protecting the hot numeric kernels (Jacobi, QRiterate, Trianglelise, DivideAndSolve) that dominate this eigensystem benchmark. FLA gets the highest SecurityGain because flattening the large control-flow-heavy functions yields the biggest structural reverse-engineering barrier at moderate cost; BCF and IBR are kept moderately weighted since opaque predicates and branch rewriting add good diversity but their runtime and size costs matter in tight floating-point loops, so their RuntimeCost/SizeCost weights are capped at 0.4-0.5. SUB is cheap, safe, and effective on arithmetic-heavy eigenvalue code, so it keeps high security/diversity weight with minimal cost weights, and SPLIT similarly adds cheap structural diversity. ICALL and IGV remain enabled at moderate security weight with elevated CorrectnessRisk weights (0.25-0.3) so the selector avoids applying indirect dispatch to functions with complex calling contexts, limiting correctness exposure while still degrading static call-graph recovery.
